text: Minutes ~ Capitol Correspondents Association Annual Meeting Jan. 16, 2020 ~ Capitol press room 1. Welcome. Meeting began at 12:56 p.m. on Thursday, Jan. 16, 2020 (Original start time of 12:15 was delayed due to House floor action re expulsion of Rep. John Green; with House in caucus and reconvening possible at any time, we shifted agenda to take up action items requiring a vote first.) In attendance: Betsy Russell, Joan Cartan-Hansen, Nate Brown, Devon Downey, Keith Ridler, Sharon Fisher, James Dawson, Logan Finney, Riley Hahn, Clark Corbin, Kevin Richert, Madison Hardy, Ryan Blake, Jeff Tucker 2. Approval of Minutes for 2019. Nate moved to approve the minutes as submitted, and Keith seconded the motion. The motion carried unanimously. 3. Election of Officers. The terms for standing committee members Kevin and Melissa are up. Clark moved to re-elect both; Devon seconded the motion, and it carried unanimously. 4. Financial report. January 1, 2020 balance is $1,274.93 Joan moved to approve the financial report; Clark seconded the motion; it passed unanimously. 5. Discussion of possible sound booth in Capitol press room. At Betsy’s request, James discussed possibilities for installing a sound booth in the press room to record and for quiet phone interviews (or any other use desired by Capitol correspondents). It would be something that could be moved if needed and something we would save to purchase, making sure we leave an adequate balance in the account. A general discussion ensued. No action will be taken until funds are available, but there was a general consensus that installing a sound booth is a good idea. Saving up for it likely would take us 2-3 years. In the meantime, quiet space for recording is available in the Idaho Public TV space under the JRW Building, down the tunnels from the Capitol; just check in with Devon. 6. Media Access concerns. Betsy asked if anyone was having access issues. Jeff Tucker explained why “Legislature Live” was having some streaming problems and hopes that they have solved most issues. James related that there were some streams with only one channel of audio. Jeff says he will investigate. Sharon asked if Betsy could talk to leadership about making sure the Ways & Means committee meets in a room with streaming. Betsy invited members to see her to share any concerns or other issues about access as they arise. 7. President’s Report. Betsy reminded everyone about the WIFI passwords and the other information, including media access rules in the Capitol, that are posted in the press room. She asked those who have not paid their dues to do so online via the Idaho Press Club website. She shared recent contacts with leadership regarding photographing from Senate private gallery (allowed with brown tag, just ask the security guard; the new guard has now been educated that this is allowed) and access to RS’s after they’re introduced in committee (Senate committee chairs will be reminded about this at their upcoming chairs meeting, Sen. Hill assures us, after Sen. Heider seemed to have forgotten that RS’s become public). Betsy invited everyone to be sure to enter their work in the IPC contest; the deadline is Jan. 22. 8. Motion to Adjourn. Sharon moved, James seconded. Motion passed. Adjournment at 1:15 p.m.
